events.content:
I want a small Next.js app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

message.content:
I want a small Next.js app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

events.content:
The app is built. I ran it in a real browser and everything you asked for works: adding books, the reading and finished lists, marking books finished, the book pages and sharing links. The books were still there after a server restart.

**To run it:** `npm run dev` (or `npm run build && npm start`), then open http://localhost:3000.

**What it does:**
- **Home page:** shows "Currently reading", then "Finished" (newest first), then a form to add a book with title, author and optional notes. Each book you're reading has a **Mark finished** button.
- **Book page** (`/books/<id>`): shows the title, author, whether you're reading it or the date you finished, and your notes with their line breaks kept. It has a **Copy link** button and a mark-finished button.
- **Sharing:** every book has its own address, so a link you send opens straight to that book. Since there are no accounts, anyone with the link can see it.
- **Saving:** books are stored in `data/books.json`, which is created the first time you add one. Saves can't half-write the file if the app crashes, and two quick submissions can't overwrite each other.

**Choices I made for you:**
- **Data file not in git:** I added `data/` to `.gitignore` so your reading list stays out of the repository. Take that line out if you'd rather commit it.
- **Hard-to-guess links:** each book gets a long random ID, so people you send a link to can't find your other books by changing the number. Anyone who can reach the app at all can still see and change everything, which is fine on your own machine but worth knowing before you put it online.
- **Form checks:** a book needs a title and an author, and there are length limits on each field.
- **No editing or deleting:** you didn't ask for these, so the only change you can make to a book is marking it finished.

**Tests:** `npm test` runs 5 tests on the saving code, including that 20 books added at the same moment are all kept. All 5 pass, and `npm run build` completes without errors.

**Worth knowing:**
- `npm audit` reports 3 security warnings, all in the `vitest` test tool that was already in the project, not in Next.js or React. Fixing them means a major upgrade of vitest, which I didn't do.
- To test in a browser I installed Playwright in `/tmp/pw` and some Chromium system libraries with `dnf`. None of that is part of the project.
- I haven't committed anything.

- **Book page** (`/books/<id>`): shows the title, author, whether you're reading it or the date you finished, and your notes with their line breaks kept. It has a **Copy link** button and a mark-finished button.
- **Sharing:** every book has its own address, so a link you send opens straight to that book. Since there are no accounts, anyone with the link can see it.
- **Saving:** books are stored in `data/books.json`, which is created the first time you add one. Saves can't half-write the file if the app crashes, and two quick submissions can't overwrite each other.

**Choices I made for you:**
- **Data file not in git:** I added `data/` to `.gitignore` so your reading list stays out of the repository. Take that line out if you'd rather commit it.
- **Hard-to-guess links:** each book gets a long random ID, so people you send a link to can't find your other books by changing the number. Anyone who can reach the app at all can still see and change everything, which is fine on your own machine but worth knowing before you put it online.
- **Form checks:** a book needs a title and an author, and there are length limits on each field.
- **No editing or deleting:** you didn't ask for these, so the only change you can make to a book is marking it finished.

**Tests:** `npm test` runs 5 tests on the saving code, including that 20 books added at the same moment are all kept. All 5 pass, and `npm run build` completes without errors.

**Worth knowing:**
- `npm audit` reports 3 security warnings, all in the `vitest` test tool that was already in the project, not in Next.js or React. Fixing them means a major upgrade of vitest, which I didn't do.
- To test in a browser I installed Playwright in `/tmp/pw` and some Chromium system libraries with `dnf`. None of that is part of the project.
- I haven't committed anything.
